A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with TinTeM renamed CosPress. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original distillation experiments covering classification, segmentation, robustness, OOD detection, specialist models, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds Proteus-VkD comparison and diagnostic results.

M1.justification: CosPress retains TinTeM's teacher head, SNE-inspired dimensionality reduction loss, cosine student loss, and concurrent training with stopped teacher-head gradients. Renaming and expanded orthogonality arguments do not alter the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is retained, including ImageNet, fine-grained classification, VOC segmentation, robustness benchmarks, OpenOOD, and specialist datasets. CIFAR-10-W and specialist OOD evaluations move to Appendix B rather than being removed.

E2.justification: v2 adds Proteus-VkD, which constrains Proteus projection matrices using VkD's reparameterisation, to the ViT-Ti/14 ImageNet comparison and component diagnostics in Tables 2–4. Other comparator memberships are retained.

E3.justification: Table 4 adds trace-based Gram-matrix deviations alongside the existing Frobenius-norm measurements. Existing classification, segmentation, robustness, training-budget, and KNN+ OOD evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 3–4 and Figure 4 extend the diagnostics to test whether right-orthogonal Proteus-VkD projections eliminate student-head information and improve orthogonality. Existing loss-weighting, loss-metric, temperature, larger-teacher, and robustness analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added Wishart calculations concern theoretical matrix properties, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation scores are retained. v2 adds Proteus-VkD results, including 73.0 kNN and 75.9 linear accuracy in Table 2, plus component scores and additional orthogonality measurements in Tables 3–4 and Figure 4.

T1.justification: v2 substantially expands the formal argument with cosine-preservation derivations, Lemma 1 relating left and right orthogonality, and Wishart-based Lemma 5 with associated proofs. The earlier JL lemmas remain, with the input-vector dimension corrected in the norm-preservation statement.

C1.justification: The principal contributions remain faithful teacher-to-student compression, improved robustness and OOD detection, and competitive specialist models on small datasets. The new title and feature-distillation terminology emphasize cosine preservation already described in v1's method and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes right-orthogonality from cosine-preserving approximate left-orthogonality and interprets Proteus-VkD's remaining errors as consequences of its matrix-exponential approximation. Existing explanations concerning training-data coverage, segmentation resolution, and specialist-model limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The code-access pointer changes from the TinTeM repository to the CosPress repository. Section 4.2 adds implementation information about Proteus-VkD's skew-symmetric, matrix-exponential reparameterisation; Table 8 drops the explicit 80GB GPU-capacity designation.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to SRD, VkD, DINOv2 Meets Text, and Scaling Vision Transformers, with targeted discussion positioning CosPress against supervised feature distillation and orthogonal projectors. The updated Proteus title and venue refer to the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method motivation are substantially rewritten. Foundation-model background moves into Related Work, method explanations are reordered, and specialist generalisation/OOD discussion moves into Appendix B. This is substantial narrative reorganisation beyond renaming.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn with explicit losses and gradient paths; Figure 4 gains Proteus-VkD curves and revised legends. Tables 2–4 are expanded, Tables 9–10 exchange order, and Tables 11–12 move to the appendix. The overall visual format remains similar.

improvement.justification: v2 adds a relevant orthogonal-projection comparison and clearer research positioning, but its new theoretical support contains a substantive flaw. Lemma 1 is false as stated: m=1, d=2, and M=[0.5,0] give sides of 1.75 and 1.25. Its proof also ends with a d/m factor absent from the stated bound (Appendix A, Eq. 37). With the original empirical evidence intact, these benefits and the theoretical regression leave the net quality change unclear.
